# The review loop of examples/review-loop, killed while the author waits in recv for the first verdict. A second beehest run continues the run.
# The killed review got the first draft and sent no verdict. After the restart, each draft reaches the reviewer once and each set of notes reaches the
# author once: the agents see the same messages, in the same order, as in the uncrashed run of review-loop.txt.
isolate
! exec bd version
! exec gh version

example review-loop/workflow.star
example review-loop/project.star config/projects/review.star
example review-loop/prompts/draft.md
example review-loop/prompts/review.md
example review-loop/prompts/revise.md
reviewfakes

exec beehestreal item add review note-1 --title 'Release note' --body-file body.txt
! exec sh first.sh run note-1 review --workflow review-loop/workflow.star &
# The review agent starts only after the reviewer received the draft, so the author has sent it. The kill also waits until the author started its recv of the verdict.
waitfile held
waitline first.err 'item-note-1-r1 step recv:verdict started'
kill -KILL
wait
cmp calls.log expected-before.log

exec beehestreal run note-1 review --workflow review-loop/workflow.star
stdout 'item note-1 finished'

exec beehestreal status
stdout 'note-1-r1\tdone'

# The author sent each draft once and received each verdict once.
exec beehestreal status item-note-1-r1
stdout -count=1 '^send:draft#1\t'
stdout -count=1 '^send:draft#2\t'
! stdout '^send:draft#3\t'
stdout -count=1 '^recv:verdict#1\t'
stdout -count=1 '^recv:verdict#2\t'
! stdout '^recv:verdict#3\t'

cmp held expected-held
cmp calls.log expected-calls.log

-- first.sh --
# The first run writes the start of each step to first.err. exec keeps the pid, so the kill stops beehest itself.
exec beehestreal "$@" 2> first.err
-- hold --
-- body.txt --
Write the release note.
-- verdicts --
changes
approve
-- expected-before.log --
draft
-- expected-held --
Draft 1.
-- expected-calls.log --
draft
review Draft 1.
revise Fix round 1.
review Draft 2.
